reference: No GNU/POSIX command implements this project-specific bl-integrity manifest-v2 API. Contract expectations use the builtin's documented interface and row layout, plus independent Python hashlib SHA-256 and BLAKE2b-512 digests for fixed byte strings. Bash type/help metadata is checked through Bash builtins.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and short help metadata
Manifest-v2 file row fields and independent SHA-256/BLAKE2b digests
Lexical row ordering, root selection, and fnmatch exclusion
Symlink row records the target text without following it
Verify success plus changed and added path reports/statuses
exclusions: No matching GNU CLI exists, so there are no parity cases; contract cases are not represented as GNU parity.
The signed/configured shell wrapper is outside this builtin's documented scope.
Default system roots are deferred because fixtures must remain relative and cannot inspect system paths.
Concurrent filesystem mutation and descriptor-pinning behavior are not exercised by fixed, data-only fixtures.

Slash-prefixed logical manifest selectors identify paths under the explicitly supplied relative --root; they are not host filesystem paths. Traversal-shaped spelling is a parser rejection contract, with no out-of-root read.

cases.purpose: Bash type and help builtins expose this enabled builtin and its documented short description.
cases.stdout:
builtin
integrity - Emit and verify bl-integrity manifest rows.

cases.purpose: The documented --version option emits the stable loadable version line.
A fixed 15-byte file produces a manifest row with the independently encoded SHA-256 and BLAKE2b-512 digests, expected mode/size/path, and numeric metadata fields.
cases.script:
umask 022
printf 'integrity test\n' > data
row=$(integrity emit-manifest --no-header --root . -- /data)
IFS=$'\t' read -r type mode size sha256 blake2b uid gid mtime ctime target path <<< "$row"
[[ $type == file && $mode == 644 && $size == 15 ]]
[[ $sha256 == c062a8490d838c777e9151bcbfdd5879e5118f99adf3ef4c5fa773455326bf1e ]]
[[ $blake2b == 4df7e29880c29c436537a89fdd37573fee8f5ffec7b1799c85b7fe048a5b2624aafd47ec151aab20695a54dc2506106811e4c976022e804f39a6449c9d901ae9 ]]
[[ $uid =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $gid =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $mtime =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $ctime =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
[[ $target == - && $path == /data ]]
printf 'file row hashes and fields verified\n'
cases.stdout: file row hashes and fields verified

cases.purpose: The default header and the standard SHA-256/BLAKE2b-512 encodings for an empty file match the manifest-v2 contract.
cases.script:
: > empty
out=$(integrity emit-manifest --root . -- /empty)
mapfile -t rows <<< "$out"
[[ ${#rows[@]} -eq 4 ]]
[[ ${rows[0]} == '# bl-integrity manifest v2' ]]
[[ ${rows[1]} == '# columns: type mode size sha256 blake2b uid gid mtime ctime target rel' ]]
[[ ${rows[2]} == '# root=.' ]]
IFS=$'\t' read -r type mode size sha256 blake2b uid gid mtime ctime target path <<< "${rows[3]}"
[[ $type == file && $mode == 644 && $size == 0 ]]
[[ $sha256 == e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 ]]
[[ $blake2b == 786a02f742015903c6c6fd852552d272912f4740e15847618a86e217f71f5419d25e1031afee585313896444934eb04b903a685b1448b755d56f701afe9be2ce ]]
[[ $target == - && $path == /empty ]]
printf 'header and empty-file digests verified\n'

cases.purpose: Selecting the root emits regular files in bytewise lexical order, while --exclude applies its documented fnmatch pattern to relative paths.
cases.script:
printf 'A\n' > alpha
printf 'B\n' > beta
printf 'G\n' > gamma
out=$(integrity emit-manifest --no-header --root . --exclude 'b*' -- /)
mapfile -t rows <<< "$out"
[[ ${#rows[@]} -eq 2 ]]
IFS=$'\t' read -r -a first <<< "${rows[0]}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r -a second <<< "${rows[1]}"
[[ ${first[0]} == file && ${first[10]} == /alpha ]]
[[ ${second[0]} == file && ${second[10]} == /gamma ]]
printf 'selection, exclusion, and ordering verified\n'

cases.purpose: A symlink to an in-root regular file is represented by its literal target and placeholder metadata; the target is separately represented as a regular file.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > target
ln -s target link
out=$(integrity emit-manifest --no-header --root . -- /link /target)
mapfile -t rows <<< "$out"
[[ ${#rows[@]} -eq 2 ]]
IFS=$'\t' read -r -a link_row <<< "${rows[0]}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r -a file_row <<< "${rows[1]}"
[[ ${link_row[0]} == symlink && ${link_row[9]} == target && ${link_row[10]} == /link ]]
[[ ${link_row[2]} == - && ${link_row[3]} == - && ${link_row[4]} == - && ${link_row[5]} == - && ${link_row[6]} == - && ${link_row[7]} == - && ${link_row[8]} == - ]]
[[ ${file_row[0]} == file && ${file_row[10]} == /target ]]
printf 'symlink recorded without following verified\n'

cases.purpose: A generated manifest verifies cleanly, then reports a changed file and an added file with status 1 and documented path labels.
cases.script:
printf 'initial\n' > original
integrity emit-manifest --no-header --root . /original > saved.manifest
if out=$(integrity verify saved.manifest --root . /original); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 && -z $out ]]
printf 'changed\n' > original
printf 'new\n' > new
if out=$(integrity verify saved.manifest --root . /original /new); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 && $out == $'changed\t/original\nadded\t/new' ]]
printf 'verify success and changed/added reports verified\n'
cases.stdout: verify success and changed/added reports verified

cases.purpose: A manifest data line without the required row fields is reported as malformed, and verification returns failure without stderr diagnostics.
cases.script:
printf 'not-a-row\n' > bad.manifest
if out=$(integrity verify bad.manifest --root . /path-that-does-not-exist); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 && $out == $'malformed\tnot-a-row' ]]
printf 'malformed row rejection verified\n'

cases.purpose: The logical path parser rejects a component-traversal spelling before walking it and returns the documented general failure status.
cases.script:
if integrity emit-manifest --no-header --root . -- /segment/../outside > metadata.out; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
printf 'traversal-shaped path rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise the implicit /bin, /bash-os, and /etc/bash-os roots against a controlled installed-system image.
cases.reason: No privilege is needed. Default roots resolve under --root (loadables/integrity.c:592-596, :643), so a relative fixture tree covers them in the legacy runner. The implicit-/ variant needs a per-side chroot built by a USERNS in the plain driver. No fixture exists.

cases.purpose: Verify an independently constructed manifest with Python hashlib/stat fields, then identify a removed entry without using candidate emission as the expected manifest.
cases.script:
printf 'independent\n' > item
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, os
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('item'); s=p.stat(); data=p.read_bytes()
fields=['file',format(s.st_mode & 0o7777,'o'),str(s.st_size),hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),hashlib.blake2b(data).hexdigest(),str(s.st_uid),str(s.st_gid),str(int(s.st_mtime)),str(int(s.st_ctime)),'-','/item']
Path('expected.manifest').write_text('\t'.join(fields)+'\n')
PY
integrity verify expected.manifest --root . /item
rm item
if integrity verify expected.manifest --root . /item; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
